Hi gang,
I'm trying to make a statistical model available to the lavaan community, given that I've developed the model on the Mplus platform. This involves putting nonlinear constraints on the loadings and involves invoking phantom variables in the place of models involved in the constraints. I'm appending the data set and the r code below. The puzzle to me is that it seems like lavaan has two estimates for the loading parameters (L1 through L16). I get slightly different numbers from lavaan than from Mplus and have tried kickstarting it with loading values close to what Mplus arrived at, but with no luck.
Initial parameters show, for example:

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Odd property of lavaan with nonlinear constraints
parts: This involves putting nonlinear constraints on the loadings

That's not what your syntax does.  You are defining new parameters using the ":=" operator.  lavaan should probably give an error when you define a new parameter with the same name as an existing one, but that is why you have a different L1 etc. among the estimates and among the defined (functions of other) estimates.

To set a constraint, use the "==" operator: 

L1 == ...

The variance-covariance matrix of the estimated parameters (vcov) does not appear to be positive definite! The smallest eigenvalue (= 7.339558e-14) is close to zero. This may be a symptom that the model is not identified.

This is not about the covariance matrix of data, but about the estimated parameters.  It happens when there is multicollinearity among estimated parameters, which I imagine can happen when some parameters are functions of others.  This happens all the time when a dummy code's mean and variance are both estimated, since the variance is a function of the mean.
